q18555.en: Motor tricycles are motor vehicles with three symmetrical wheels.

explain.short: This is the definition of a motor tricycle: three wheels placed symmetrically, so the vehicle is balanced.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'simmetriche' (symmetrical) is the key word: a motorbike with a sidecar has three wheels, but they are not symmetrical.

q18556.en: Motor tricycles are vehicles with an engine larger than 50 cm3.

explain.short: A motor tricycle has an engine over 50 cm3. With a smaller engine it would be a moped-type vehicle, not a motor tricycle.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'superiore' means 'more than': over 50 cm3 is correct for motor tricycles.

q18557.en: Motor tricycles are motor vehicles with a maximum design speed above 45 km/h.

explain.short: A motor tricycle can go faster than 45 km/h by construction. Vehicles limited to 45 km/h are mopeds.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'superiore a 45 km/h' means 'above 45 km/h': that is the motor tricycle, not the moped.

sceneParams.caption: Motor tricycle: top speed over 45 km/h

q18558.en: Motor tricycles must have a revision four years after first registration, then every two years.

explain.short: Motor tricycles follow the same revision timing as cars and motorcycles: first after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: Remember the pair of numbers 'quattro ... due' (four ... two): it is the normal revision timing.

q18559.en: Motor tricycles are motor vehicles that can be driven without a licence.

explain.short: A motor tricycle is fast (over 45 km/h) and powerful (over 50 cm3), so you always need a driving licence to drive it.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'senza patente' (without a licence) is the trap: motor tricycles always need a licence.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: a motor tricycle needs a licence

q18560.en: Motor tricycles are made up of a motorcycle and a sidecar.

explain.short: A motorcycle with a sidecar is still a motorcycle. A motor tricycle is built with three symmetrical wheels.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'sidecar' is the trap: three wheels, but not symmetrical, so it is not a motor tricycle.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: motorbike + sidecar is not a tricycle

q18561.en: Motor tricycles are vehicles with an engine under 50 cm3 and a maximum design speed up to 45 km/h.

explain.short: These numbers (under 50 cm3, up to 45 km/h) describe mopeds. Motor tricycles are above both limits.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'inferiore' (less than) and 'fino a' (up to) are the trap: motor tricycles are OVER 50 cm3 and 45 km/h.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: under 50 cm3 / 45 km/h is a moped

q18562.en: Motor tricycles are not subject to periodic revision.

explain.short: Motor tricycles do have periodic revision: first after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.rule: A motor tricycle (triciclo a motore) has three symmetrical wheels, an engine over 50 cm3 and a top speed over 45 km/h; it needs a licence and periodic revision.
explain.trap: 'non sono soggetti' (are not subject) is the trap: revision is compulsory.

q18563.en: Petrol-powered light quadricycles have an engine of 50 cm3 or less.

explain.short: A light quadricycle (quadriciclo leggero) is like a small four-wheel moped: a petrol engine of at most 50 cm3.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'inferiore o pari' means 'less than or equal': 50 cm3 itself is still allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Light quadricycle: petrol up to 50 cm3
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

explain.short: 'Quadri' means four: a quadricycle is a small motor vehicle with four wheels.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'quattro ruote' (four wheels) is just the basic definition, no hidden trick.

sceneParams.caption: Quadricycle: four wheels
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18567.en: Light quadricycles are treated like mopeds for traffic purposes.

explain.short: Light quadricycles are small and slow (max 45 km/h), so on the road they follow the moped (ciclomotore) rules.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'assimilati' means 'treated like': the light ones count as mopeds, not as motorcycles.

sceneParams.caption: Light quadricycle = like a moped
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18568.en: The power of non-light quadricycles is always 15 kW or less.

explain.short: Non-light quadricycles are bigger than light ones, but their power still has a ceiling: at most 15 kW.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'sempre' (always) is usually a warning word, but here it is right: 15 kW is the top limit.

sceneParams.caption: Non-light quadricycle: max 15 kW
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18569.en: Quadricycles are subject to periodic revision.

explain.short: Like other motor vehicles, quadricycles must have periodic revision to check they are safe.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: No trick: 'revisione periodica' (periodic official check) applies to quadricycles too.

sceneParams.caption: Quadricycles: periodic revision
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18570.en: Quadricycles other than light ones can be driven without a licence.

explain.short: Non-light quadricycles are faster and more powerful, so you need a driving licence for them.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'senza patente' (without a licence) is wrong for non-light quadricycles.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: non-light quadricycles need a licence
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18571.en: Non-light quadricycles are treated as mopeds for traffic purposes.

explain.short: Only LIGHT quadricycles count as mopeds. Non-light ones are bigger and faster and follow their own rules.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'non leggeri' (non-light) is the trap: the moped rule is only for the light ones.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: only LIGHT ones count as mopeds
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18573.en: It is allowed to replace the exhaust of light quadricycles to raise the top speed, as long as the engine size is not increased.

explain.short: You may not modify a light quadricycle to go faster. Changing the exhaust to raise the speed is forbidden.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'purché' (as long as) makes it sound acceptable, but any change to go faster is forbidden.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: no tuning to go faster
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18574.en: Driving non-light quadricycles is allowed from the age of fourteen.

explain.short: At 14 you can only drive mopeds and light quadricycles. Non-light quadricycles need an older driver with a licence.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'quattordicesimo anno' (age 14) is the age for mopeds and light quadricycles, not the non-light ones.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: 14 is for light ones only
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18575.en: Non-light quadricycles with handlebars and an open body can be driven without a helmet.

explain.short: With handlebars and an open body you are exposed like on a motorbike, so the helmet is compulsory.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'senza casco' (without a helmet) is the trap: open body plus handlebars means helmet.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: handlebars + open body = helmet
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18576.en: It is allowed to increase the engine size of light quadricycles as long as the speed is not increased.

explain.short: The engine of a light quadricycle must stay as approved. Making the cylinders bigger is forbidden, whatever the speed.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'purché' (as long as) sounds like a condition that makes it OK, but changing the engine size is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: engine size can't be increased
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18577.en: It is allowed to replace the engine of a light quadricycle to raise its top speed above 45 km/h.

explain.short: A light quadricycle must stay within 45 km/h. Replacing the engine to go faster is forbidden.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'sostituire il motore' (replace the engine) to go over 45 km/h is never allowed.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: light quadricycle stays at 45 km/h
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18578.en: Quadricycles are not subject to periodic revision.

explain.short: Quadricycles do have periodic revision, like the other motor vehicles.
explain.rule: Quadricycles have four wheels and periodic revision. Light ones (leggeri) count as mopeds; non-light ones go up to 15 kW and need a licence.
explain.trap: 'non sono soggetti' (are not subject) is the trap: revision is compulsory.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: quadricycles do have revision
lines: Light: up to 50 cm3, like a moped

q18584.en: Operating machines can be self-propelled or towed.

explain.short: Operating machines (macchine operatrici, for road and building work) can have their own engine or be towed.
explain.rule: Agricultural and operating machines are slow working vehicles; they go on the road only under strict limits (registration, low speed, no extra passengers).

q18585.en: Operating machines can be snow-clearing vehicles.

explain.short: Snow ploughs are a typical example of operating machines: they work on the road to keep it clear.
explain.rule: Agricultural and operating machines are slow working vehicles; they go on the road only under strict limits (registration, low speed, no extra passengers).

q18586.en: Operating machines can travel at a speed above 50 km/h.

explain.short: Operating machines are slow work vehicles: they may never go faster than 40 km/h, so 50 km/h is far too much.
explain.rule: Agricultural and operating machines are slow working vehicles; they go on the road only under strict limits (registration, low speed, no extra passengers).

q18587.en: Tracked operating machines can travel at a speed above 45 km/h.

explain.short: Machines on tracks are the slowest of all: they must stay at very low speeds, far below 45 km/h.
explain.rule: Agricultural and operating machines are slow working vehicles; they go on the road only under strict limits (registration, low speed, no extra passengers).

q18594.en: Caravans are trailers equipped to be used as living quarters.

explain.short: A caravan is towed by a car and is fitted out like a small home.

q18595.en: Caravans can be used as living quarters only when the vehicle is stationary.

explain.rule: A caravan (roulotte) is a trailer equipped as a home; people may stay in it only when it is parked.

q18597.en: It is possible to stay in caravans while travelling.

q18599.en: Caravans are trailers intended exclusively for carrying tourist and sports equipment.

explain.short: Heavy lorries and trailers over 3.5 t also need reflective stripes at the back and on the sides, so their size is visible at night.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'posteriori e laterali' (rear and side): both are required.

sceneParams.caption: Over 3.5 t: rear and side stripes

q18613.en: The panel shown indicates the transport of dangerous goods.

explain.short: The orange panel with two numbers marks dangerous goods: the top number shows the danger, the bottom one the substance.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'merci pericolose' (dangerous goods) is right for the orange numbered panel.

q18614.en: The panel shown indicates the transport of loads sticking out.

explain.short: The square panel with red and white diagonal stripes is placed at the end of a load that sticks out of the vehicle.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'carichi sporgenti' (loads sticking out) is right for the square red-and-white panel.

q18615.en: The reflective stripes applied to the sides of some vehicles can be white or yellow.

explain.short: Side stripes on heavy vehicles are white or yellow. Red is used only at the back.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'lateralmente' (on the sides) is the key: sides are white or yellow.

q18616.en: The reflective stripes applied to the back of some vehicles can be red or yellow.

explain.short: Rear stripes on heavy vehicles are red or yellow, the colours we expect to see at the back of a vehicle.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'dietro' (at the back) is the key: rear stripes are red or yellow.

q18617.en: A driver who sees the panels shown is following a lorry with a laden mass over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: Yellow panels with red diagonal stripes mean the vehicle ahead is a lorry over 3.5 t.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'autocarro' (lorry) is right: diagonal stripes = lorry, red border = trailer.

sceneParams.caption: Diagonal stripes ahead: a lorry > 3.5 t

q18618.en: A driver who sees the panels shown is following a trailer or semi-trailer for goods with a laden mass over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: Yellow panels with a red border mean the vehicle ahead is a goods trailer or semi-trailer over 3.5 t.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'rimorchio o semirimorchio' (trailer or semi-trailer) is right for the red-border panel.

sceneParams.caption: Red border ahead: a trailer > 3.5 t

q18619.en: Side reflective stripes must be applied to lorries with a total laden mass below 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: Reflective stripes are compulsory only on vehicles OVER 3.5 t, not on lighter ones.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'inferiore' (below) is the trap: the rule is for vehicles over 3.5 t.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: stripes are for OVER 3.5 t

q18620.en: While travelling, lorries with a total laden mass of 3.5 tonnes or less must be marked at the rear with yellow and red reflective panels.

explain.short: The yellow and red rear panels are for heavy vehicles OVER 3.5 t. Lorries up to 3.5 t do not need them.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'inferiore o uguale' (3.5 t or less) is the trap: the panels are for heavier vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: panels are for OVER 3.5 t

q18621.en: A sign showing the minimum allowed speed must be displayed on the back of buses.

explain.short: Buses do not carry a 'minimum speed' sign at the back. No vehicle shows its minimum speed.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'velocità minima' (minimum speed) is invented: there is no such sign on buses.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: no minimum-speed sign on buses
lines: No vehicle shows a minimum speed

q18622.en: A sign showing the maximum allowed speed must be displayed on the back of cars.

explain.short: Normal cars (autovetture) do not need a speed sign at the back. Speed discs are for some heavy vehicles.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'autovetture' (cars) is the trap: cars carry no such sign.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: cars have no speed sign at the back
lines: Cars: no speed sign at the back

q18623.en: Caravans must have red or yellow reflective stripes at the rear.

explain.short: Reflective stripes are required on goods vehicles over 3.5 t. A caravan is a trailer for living in, not a heavy goods vehicle.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'caravan (roulottes)' is the trap: the stripe rule is for heavy goods vehicles.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: stripes are for goods vehicles > 3.5 t

q18624.en: Buses must have red or white reflective stripes at the rear.

explain.short: White is a side colour and the stripe rule is for goods vehicles over 3.5 t, not buses. Rear stripes are red or yellow.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'rosso o bianco' (red or white) is wrong: white never goes at the back.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: rear stripes are red or yellow

q18625.en: The panel shown is fitted at the rear of trailers or semi-trailers with a laden mass over 3.5 tonnes.

explain.short: The panel with red diagonal stripes is for lorries. Trailers and semi-trailers carry the yellow panel with a red border.
explain.rule: Heavy goods vehicles over 3.5 t must carry reflective rear panels and reflective stripes, so other drivers see them well, also at night.
explain.trap: 'rimorchi o semirimorchi' (trailers) is the trap: this diagonal-stripe panel belongs to lorries.

explain.short: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a motor vehicle with two wheels.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: No trick: 'due ruote' (two wheels) is part of the definition.

q18627.en: Motorcycles have an engine larger than 50 cm3.

explain.short: Above 50 cm3 a two-wheeler is a motorcycle; up to 50 cm3 it is a moped.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'superiore' (more than) is right: motorcycles are over 50 cm3.

q18628.en: Mopeds are not part of the motorcycle category.

explain.short: Mopeds (ciclomotori: up to 50 cm3, up to 45 km/h) are a separate category from motorcycles.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'non rientrano' (are not included) is right: mopeds and motorcycles are different.

q18629.en: Motorcycles can be fitted with an automatic gearbox.

explain.short: Many motorcycles and scooters have an automatic gearbox; it is fully allowed.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'possono' (can) is right: automatic gearbox is possible, not compulsory.

q18630.en: Motorcycles must have a revision four years after first registration, then every two years.

explain.short: Motorcycles follow the normal timing: first revision after 4 years, then every 2 years.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: Remember 'quattro ... due' (four ... two): the normal revision timing.

q18631.en: All motor vehicles with three wheels are motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorcycles have two wheels. Three-wheelers can be motor tricycles or three-wheel mopeds.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'Tutti' (all) and 'tre ruote' (three wheels) are the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: three wheels is not a motorcycle

q18632.en: Motorcycles are motor vehicles with more than two wheels.

explain.short: A motorcycle has exactly two wheels, not more.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'più di due ruote' (more than two wheels) is the trap.

q18633.en: A motorcycle is any two-wheeled vehicle.

explain.short: Bicycles and mopeds also have two wheels but are not motorcycles. A motorcycle needs an engine over 50 cm3.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'qualunque' (any) is the trap: not every two-wheeler is a motorcycle.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: bikes and mopeds are not motorcycles

q18634.en: Only two-wheeled vehicles with an engine up to 125 cm3 are defined as motorcycles.

explain.short: Motorcycles start above 50 cm3 and have no upper limit. 125 cm3 is only a licence limit (A1), not the definition.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'solo' (only) and 'fino a 125 cm3' (up to 125 cm3) are the trap.

sceneParams.caption: Wrong: no 125 cm3 limit for motorcycles

q18635.en: Motorcycles have an engine up to 50 cm3 and reach a speed up to 45 km/h.

explain.short: Up to 50 cm3 and 45 km/h describes a moped. Motorcycles are over 50 cm3.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'fino a 50 cm3' and 'fino a 45 km/h' are moped numbers, not motorcycle numbers.

q18636.en: For traffic purposes, light quadricycles are treated like motorcycles.

explain.short: Light quadricycles are treated like MOPEDS (ciclomotori), not like motorcycles.
explain.rule: A motorcycle (motociclo) is a two-wheel motor vehicle with an engine over 50 cm3; it is not a moped.
explain.trap: 'motocicli' (motorcycles) is the swapped word: the right one is 'ciclomotori' (mopeds).
